350°F The cut depends on the food, so one number is never the whole answer. Each cell gives the air fryer temperature, °C, gas mark and the share of the oven time you save. Food Basket Oven-style General / mixed 325°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 20% less time 330°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 15% less time Fries & potatoes 325°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 30% less time 330°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 25% less time Chicken wings 325°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 20% less time 330°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 15% less time Chicken breast (boneless) 325°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 25% less time 330°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 20% less time Chicken thighs / bone-in 325°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 20% less time 330°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 15% less time Steak & thick cuts 330°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 20% less time 335°F / 170°C Gas mark 3 · 15% less time Fish & salmon 330°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 20% less time 335°F / 170°C Gas mark 3 · 15% less time Bacon 325°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 30% less time 330°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 25% less time Vegetables 325°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 25% less time 330°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 20% less time Baked goods & cookies 330°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 15% less time 335°F / 170°C Gas mark 3 · 10% less time Pizza & reheating 325°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 25% less time 330°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 20% less time Casseroles & thick bakes 330°F / 165°C Gas mark 3 · 15% less time 335°F / 170°C Gas mark 3 · 10% less time What recipes use 350°F 350°F (175°C, gas mark 4) is the default for anything that has to set in the middle before the outside darkens: muffins, quick breads, brownies, cookies, cheesecake, meatloaf, baked pasta and most casseroles. It is also where older recipes land when the writer was not sure, so plenty of chicken and pork recipes say 350°F for an hour when they would brown better hotter. The recipes that use this temperature are the ones that suffer most when an air fryer is treated as a small oven. A flat rule turns every one of them into 325°F, but baked goods and casseroles take a smaller cut: a dense batter or a deep dish needs the heat to reach its centre, and the gentler number stops the crust from setting first. The failure mode at 350°F: done outside, raw inside At this heat the problem is not burning, it is speed on the surface. The fan blows straight onto the top of a muffin or a cake, which browns and crusts while the middle is still liquid. The result is a domed, cracked top over a gummy centre, and adding time only darkens the top further. Three things fix it. Use a shallower pan than the recipe calls for, so the centre has less distance to cover. Tent the top loosely with foil for the first half of the cook, tucking the edges under the pan so the fan cannot lift it. And test the middle with a skewer at the check time instead of trusting the colour. Paper and foil liners must be weighed down by the food; a loose sheet will lift into the element at any temperature. Worked example A muffin recipe says 350°F for 20 minutes. Baked goods get one of the smallest cuts in the table, so a basket air fryer runs them at 330°F (165°C) for 17 minutes, and you should test with a skewer at 12 minutes. An oven-style unit blows less directly onto the tops, so it takes 335°F for 18 minutes. Bake in silicone or paper cups set in the basket, filled halfway rather than to the brim. Converting 350°F to °C and gas mark 350°F is 175°C rounded to the nearest five, which is how most European recipes print it, and gas mark 4. In the air fryer the general setting is 325°F, or 165°C — gas mark 3 if you are reading the result against a UK recipe. Many air fryers sold in Europe step in 10°C rather than 5°C. If yours does, round down for cakes and casseroles and up for chicken: the dense foods are safe from a dark crust and the poultry gets the extra colour. The converter accepts °C directly if your recipe started there. For a general recipe, 325°F (165°C) in a basket air fryer with about 20% less time, or 330°F in an oven-style unit. Cakes, casseroles, steak and fish take a smaller cut; the table above lists every food. What is 350°F in Celsius for an air fryer? 350°F is 175°C. Converted for a basket air fryer it becomes 165°C. If your air fryer only shows °C, enter the recipe in °C in the converter and it does both steps at once. How much shorter is the air fryer time at 350°F? About 20% shorter for most foods in a basket unit. Fries and bacon save the most, cakes and casseroles the least. The first time you cook a recipe, check at the time the converter shows rather than waiting for the end, since basket size and wattage vary. Can I bake a cake in an air fryer at 350°F? Yes, but use the converted temperature rather than 350°F, and a pan that leaves space around its sides for air. Cover the top loosely with foil if it browns before a skewer comes out clean. A cake deeper than about 5 cm is better in the oven. Why not just subtract 25°F from 350°F? Because it is only right for some foods. A flat 25°F works for chicken and general recipes, but dense batters and deep casseroles need the heat to reach the middle and get a smaller cut — the difference between a set centre and a raw one.
